tagline: Down the Klamath and over Grayback into Oregon.
intro: From Yreka the byway takes Highway 263 north over five Pioneer bridges to Highway 96, then follows the Klamath River west to Happy Camp. There it turns north up Indian Creek toward its headwaters, climbs over the 5,000-foot Grayback summit through old Brewer spruce forest, and comes down to US 199 at O'Brien, Oregon. It is 108 miles end to end.

The name dates from November 1941, when young men with hunting rifles stopped traffic on US 99 south of Yreka and handed out a proclamation. The State of Jefferson, it said, was in rebellion against California and Oregon and would "secede every Thursday until further notice."

moments.title: Seiad Valley
moments.text: About 300 people live along the Klamath here under the three craggy peaks of the Lower Devils, and the Pacific Crest Trail passes through the west side of the valley.

moments.title: Happy Camp
moments.text: The Heart of the Klamath. By one account the miner Jack Titus named it after his partner, James Camp, arrived and called it the happiest day of his life.

moments.title: O'Brien
moments.text: The road ends at a few businesses on US 199 in the valley of the West Fork Illinois River, five miles inside Oregon.

practical: The Grayback road over to Oregon is a seasonal summer road and is not cleared or maintained in snow.
